questions.question:
Section One: Oscillatory motion
1. Define Amplitude and state its SI-Unit. [ 2 marks ]
questions.answer_guide: Amplitude is the maximum displacement of a vibrating particle from its rest (equilibrium) position. SI unit: metre (m).

questions.section: Part three: Direct questions and problems [ 50 marks ]
questions.question:
Section Two: Wave motion
1. Differentiate Between Mechanical wave and electromagnetic wave. [ 2 marks]
questions.answer_guide: Mechanical waves need a material medium to travel (e.g. sound, water waves); electromagnetic waves do not need a medium and can travel through a vacuum at 3 × 10⁸ m/s (e.g. light, radio waves).

questions.section: Part three: Direct questions and problems [ 50 marks ]
questions.question:
Section Three: Sound Waves
1. Can Sound Travel through a vacuum (empty space)? Explain your answer [ 3 marks]
questions.answer_guide: No. Sound is a mechanical (longitudinal) wave that needs particles of a medium to vibrate and pass on the energy; a vacuum has no particles.

questions.section: Part three: Direct questions and problems [ 50 marks ]
questions.question:
Section Four: Reflection of light
1. An object 5cm high is placed at a distance of 10cm from a convex mirror of radius 30cm. find:
  a) The position of the image [ 3 marks]
  b) The nature of the image [ 1 mark]
  c) Size of the image [2 marks]
questions.answer_guide:
f = −R/2 = −15 cm (convex); 1/v = 1/f − 1/u = −1/15 − 1/10 = −1/6 → v = −6 cm (6 cm behind the mirror)
b) Virtual, upright (erect) and diminished.
c) m = |v|/u = 6/10 = 0.6 → image height = 0.6 × 5 = 3 cm

questions.section: Part three: Direct questions and problems [ 50 marks ]
questions.question:
Section Five: Refraction of Light
1. State Snell's law of refraction [ 3 marks]
questions.answer_guide: For two given media, the ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence to the sine of the angle of refraction is constant: sin i / sin r = n (refractive index). The incident ray, refracted ray and normal all lie in the same plane.

questions.section: Part three: Direct questions and problems [ 50 marks ]
questions.question:
Section Six: Dispersion of Light
1. If you look at the sky in a day without clouds, you can see it as blue in color, so why the sky is Blue? [3 marks]
questions.answer_guide: Sunlight is scattered by gas molecules in the atmosphere; short-wavelength blue light is scattered much more than longer wavelengths (Rayleigh scattering), so blue light reaches our eyes from all directions of the sky.

Section Nine: Basic electronics
1. List the types of transistors [ 2 marks]
questions.answer_guide: NPN and PNP (bipolar junction transistors); also field-effect transistors (FET).

questions.section: Part three: Direct questions and problems [ 50 marks ]
questions.question:
Section Nine: Basic electronics
2. Differentiate between extrinsic and intrinsic semiconductors [ 2 marks]
questions.answer_guide: An intrinsic semiconductor is a pure semiconductor (e.g. pure silicon or germanium). An extrinsic semiconductor has been doped with impurities to increase conductivity (n-type or p-type).

Section Ten: Modern physics
1. Blue light has a wavelength of 7.7 × 10¹⁴HZ and Planck's constant is 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ js. Calculate the energy of the light. [ 3 marks]
questions.answer_guide:
(The value given is a frequency, f = 7.7 × 10¹⁴ Hz.)
E = hf = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ × 7.7 × 10¹⁴ ≈ 5.1 × 10⁻¹⁹ J
